name: Drua Sailing Experience
subtitle: Serviceable 24 V solar workshop with two-string battery resilience

currency.note: Planning rate retained from the source workbook; use the actual purchase-date rate.

budget.note: Panels, batteries and the UniFi Express are included in the project total even though they have already been purchased. The estimated $607.11 Ekrano GX increment, net of the $80 list-price saving from using a non-GX rather than GX 24 V MultiPlus and including the estimated border-tax effect, is donor-funded. Victron power-electronics costs are current planning prices pending a same-part-number Solar Fiji quote. Freight beyond Nadi, panel mounting, Starlink hardware and labor are excluded.

summary: Four 565 W panels form two matched two-panel series strings (2S2P) and feed a Victron SmartSolar 150/85 through two separate 4 mm² positive/negative home runs. At the assumed 15 m one-way distance, the two runs lose about 2.0% at rated power; a documented one-run fallback accepts about 4.0% loss only after an array-side combiner and cable-ampacity check. Four 12 V GEL batteries form two independently fused 24 V series strings used together through a compact 1 / 2 / BOTH / OFF selector. If one battery fails, its whole two-battery string can be isolated while the other preserves essential service at half capacity. A non-GX Victron MultiPlus-II provides AC and generator charging, while the Ekrano GX coordinates charge current, local monitoring and VRM reporting. A protected 24-to-12 V branch keeps Starlink, UniFi, lights and USB online with the inverter off.

powerModel.assumptions: 4.2 peak-sun-hours, 75% solar derate, 50% GEL depth of discharge, one power tool at a time, about 0.10 kWh/day for the always-on Ekrano GX with its display normally asleep, and 15 m one-way copper PV runs. PV cable loss uses 0.01724 Ω·mm²/m copper resistivity at 20°C; field temperature raises resistance, so confirm the actual route and cable before purchase.

batteryCablePlan.conductor: 1/0 AWG (53.5 mm²) UL 1426 flexible tinned-copper marine battery cable
batteryCablePlan.procurement: Import factory-crimped, adhesive-heat-shrunk assemblies; no heavy-cable crimper is required on site.
batteryCablePlan.measurementRule: Buy only after a 1:1 component layout. Measure hole-to-hole along the supported route, preserve broad bend radii, and keep the paired A/B paths equal. Confirm every stud before ordering, especially the purchased EverExceed battery terminals and final busbars.

components.summary: Two matched two-panel series strings wired in parallel at the protected building entry (2S2P).
components.note: Confirm every module nameplate is STP565S-C72/Vmh or electrically identical before wiring.

components.summary: First module in two-panel series string A.

components.title: Panel 2
components.summary: Second module in string A; its string output gets a dedicated 4 mm² positive/negative home run.

components.summary: First module in two-panel series string B.

components.title: Panel 4
components.summary: Second module in string B; its string output gets a dedicated 4 mm² positive/negative home run.
specs: Protected parallel combination at building entry

components.title: PV protection + combine
components.summary: A configurable weatherproof array box protects and identifies both strings; at the building entry, protected terminals parallel the two runs ahead of surge protection and a common disconnect.
specs: Entry: Type 2 PV SPD coordinated with 150 V MPPT
60 m single-core cable total at 15 m one-way
components.note: Each string can sit near 105 VDC in cool sunlight. Cover modules before connector work; never break MC4 connectors under load. The one-run contingency requires combining at the array in a weatherproof protected box—do not substitute an improvised MC4 Y lead—and confirming that the actual 4 mm² cable and installation method are rated for at least the combined design current.

components.title: SmartSolar MPPT 150/85-Tr
components.summary: A separate Victron charger keeps solar charging and essential DC services independent of the AC inverter/charger.
specs: 150 V absolute maximum PV Voc · 145 V operating maximum
2,400 W nominal PV capacity at 24 V
components.note: The 2S strings model at 104.7 V cold Voc, leaving about 40 V below the 145 V operating ceiling. Fit the matching WireBox-XL Tr, mount terminals down within 3 m of the battery bus, and use a 100 A output fuse with 10 cm ventilation clearance. Set the charger itself to 85 A maximum and let Ekrano DVCC cap the combined system charge current.

components.title: MultiPlus-II 24/3000
components.summary: The non-GX model provides the same inverter, generator charger and transfer-switch capability while leaving the Ekrano GX as the system's single monitoring and control device.
components.note: Do not substitute the MultiPlus-II GX version when installing the Ekrano. IP22 and 95% non-condensing are not salt-spray ratings: mount in the dry, ventilated inner room behind the drip/salt shield, away from sea-facing openings and batteries.

components.title: Ekrano GX
components.summary: The system's only GX device combines a bright local touchscreen with coordinated DVCC control, collects inverter, solar and battery data, and sends monitoring and alarms to Victron VRM through the UniFi Express and Starlink.
specs: Front IP54 with steel bracket · rear IP21
components.note: Power directly from the protected 24 V bus on the system side of the SmartShunt—not from AC output or the low-voltage-controlled load branch—so it can report faults and recovery. Install horizontally through the flat junction-box door with the supplied rear steel bracket and compressed seal; the spring-clip method is only IP31. Keep its rear connectors inside the dry enclosure and hardwire Ethernet to the UniFi LAN port.

components.title: 24 V · 400 Ah GEL bank
components.summary: 9.6 kWh nominal, operated to about 50% depth of discharge for longer GEL life.
specs: One string: 4.8 kWh nominal · 2.4 kWh usable
components.note: Fully charge and voltage-match all four units separately before assembly. Keep the two strings electrically independent up to the selector so either pair can be isolated without dismantling the healthy pair.

components.title: Battery 1
components.summary: Lower battery in the first 24 V series string.

components.title: Battery 2
components.summary: Upper battery in the first 24 V series string.

components.title: Battery 3
components.summary: Lower battery in the second 24 V series string.

components.title: Battery 4

components.title: Main DC distribution
components.summary: Covered 300 A-class busbars distribute the selector output to the inverter, 100 A solar-charger branch and 30 A DC-services branch; all negative current crosses the SmartShunt.
specs: Two 150 A Class T string fuses
components.note: Put each Class T fuse as close as practicable to its string-positive terminal. The two 150 A protected feeds provide 300 A aggregate protection in BOTH mode; one-string mode is intentionally reduced-capability. Nothing except the two battery-string negatives connects on the BATTERY MINUS side of the shunt. Import all heavy 1/0 AWG assemblies preterminated after a 1:1 layout so no field crimper is required.

components.title: String selector
components.summary: A compact Blue Sea 6007 selector normally combines both protected 24 V strings and lets operators isolate either string after a battery fault.
components.note: Mount through a fixed internal faceplate—not the hinged door—so three heavy 1/0 AWG cables never flex when the box opens. The switch is rated only 25 A while changing position: stop AC loads, disable inverter/charger, isolate PV and generator charging, then change position. Operate in BOTH normally; use 1 or 2 only after identifying the healthy string.

components.title: 2 × battery balancers
components.summary: Each two-battery string gets its own Victron balancer so the strings remain independently serviceable.
specs: Two units for two series pairs
Alarm relay from each unit to one Ekrano digital input

components.title: Existing G3200P
components.summary: Retained for cloudy spells and emergency charging; not part of normal daily operation.
components.note: Acceptance of a non-inverter generator is not guaranteed. Test voltage, frequency, earth arrangement and charger acceptance before relying on it.

components.title: Generator inlet
components.summary: Weather-protected inlet, three-core lead and two-pole input isolation feed the MultiPlus AC input.
components.note: Included because the incremental hardware is below the user's $250 ceiling.

components.title: AC output protection
components.summary: Small plywood-mounted enclosure with a two-pole 10 A / 30 mA Type A RCBO feeding one flexible tool lead; no receptacle is fixed to the building wall.
specs: MultiPlus AC-out L / N / PE hardwired
components.note: The RCBO and continuous protective-earth path remain required even though the outlet is movable. A qualified electrical person must verify neutral-earth behavior in inverter and generator/bypass modes.

components.title: Trailing tool lead
components.summary: A short heavy-duty three-core flexible cable ends in one rugged Fiji Type I trailing socket, avoiding fixed outlets on metal or thatched walls.
specs: 10 A Type I trailing socket · IP44 minimum
components.note: Fully uncoil the lead before tool use, keep it dry and away from sharp metal or thatch, and hang it beside the equipment when stored. No power boards, daisy chains, kettle or second tool.

components.title: Victron Orion-Tr 24/12-30A
components.summary: An isolated Victron converter runs essential services while the AC inverter is off and keeps the 12 V wiring inside one supported equipment family.
components.note: Keep combined 12 V loads below 300 W continuous for heat margin. Use its configurable input-voltage lockout in power-supply mode as the GEL low-voltage control; commission approximately 24.0 V lockout and 25.0 V restart under real load rather than adding a separate BatteryProtect.

components.title: 12 V fused distribution
components.summary: A common positive rail feeds six fuse ways; each red load conductor leaves through its own fuse while every black load conductor returns unfused to a separate negative bus.
specs: 35 A converter output fuse ahead of the block
components.note: Do not place a fuse or switch in any 12 V negative return. Orion output negative and every load negative land on the negative-return bus; only positive conductors pass through branch fuses.

components.title: Essential 12 V services
components.summary: Starlink Mini, UniFi Wi-Fi, LED lighting and USB charging.
components.note: Starlink hardware itself is outside the project purchase scope.

components.title: USB charging station

Fits inside either iM2875 with padding

Use factory-crimped tinned lugs, adhesive heat-shrink, noncorroding hardware and bottom cable entries; prove component depth, terminal access, route length and the 14.4 mm cable bend envelope at 1:1 scale before ordering cables or drilling the purchased enclosure.

Primary design: two independent 15 m one-way string home runs, each with a positive and negative conductor (4 conductors × 15 m = 60 m single-core total). At STC and 20°C copper resistance, each string loses about 22.8 W and both together lose 45.6 W / 2.02%. If only 30 m is available, use the documented protected array-side combining configuration and one positive/negative run; expect about 91.2 W / 4.04% loss and first confirm the actual cable's installed ampacity is at least 40 A. bom.description: Factory-crimped UL 1426 flexible tinned-copper 1/0 AWG (53.5 mm²) assemblies with tinned lugs and adhesive heat-shrink; this meets Victron's 50 mm² requirement for a 24/3000 connection up to 5 m and avoids buying a heavy-cable crimper. The current configurator prices these twelve assemblies at about $251.52 plus $3.97 U.S. shipping, rounded here to $260 before any applicable sales tax. At the vendor's published 0.424 lb/ft, the 24 ft planning set weighs about 10.2 lb. operatingRules: Keep both PV strings on their separate 4 mm² positive/negative home runs in normal service. The one-run arrangement is a cable-shortage contingency only: combine in the protected array box, verify the actual cable and route are rated for at least 40 A, label the change at both ends, and expect about 4% cable loss instead of 2%.

Use one corded power tool at a time from the dedicated trailing socket and keep the tool nameplate at or below about 1,800 W. Fully uncoil and inspect the lead before use; do not add a power board, daisy-chain another extension, or combine the saw with the planer, jigsaw, drill, kettle or another large AC load. Hang the lead dry beside the equipment after use.
Run tool work mainly in sunny hours. Stop tool loads around 50% state of charge; reserve the lower half of the GEL bank for longevity and essentials.
Keep the AC inverter off when no AC loads are required. Starlink, UniFi, USB and lights continue on the protected 12 V branch.
Leave the Ekrano GX powered so it can retain battery history and report alarms. Let its display time out when not in use; investigate alarms locally before resetting them.
Operate the battery selector in BOTH during normal service. Never change it under load or while solar, generator charging or the inverter/charger is active.

If a battery or balancer alarm identifies a bad string: stop AC loads, disable inverter/charger, isolate PV and generator input, move the selector to the healthy string, reduce the Ekrano DVCC charge-current limit from 100 A to 50 A, then restore essentials. Treat one-string operation as limp mode: no saw or other high-surge workshop load until both strings are healthy.
Never equalize GEL batteries. Inspect individual battery voltage, temperature, swelling, torque and corrosion monthly.

Keep all power electronics dry and away from direct salt air. Every three months, isolate the system, inspect for salt deposits or corrosion, clean/replace the alcove filter and correct any moisture source.
Treat the generator as tested backup only. Confirm the MultiPlus accepts its voltage/frequency and verify RCD/earth behavior before relying on charging or bypass.
commissioning: Confirm all four panel and battery nameplates before terminating anything.

Before ordering the imported heavy-cable set, buy or fix the exact Class T holders, selector, SmartShunt and M10 busbars; then make a full-size battery/box/MultiPlus layout from actual hardware and battery dimensions. Confirm the EverExceed terminal is M8, measure each supported route hole-to-hole, preserve broad bends, and keep the paired A/B positive and negative paths equal. Order the 12 UL 1426 tinned-copper 1/0 AWG assemblies factory-crimped with tinned lugs and adhesive heat-shrink; no site crimping is planned.
Separately fully charge and voltage-match the four batteries. Build two matched 24 V strings, install one balancer per string, and land each balancer alarm relay on its own Ekrano digital input.

Fit a 150 A Class T fuse close to each string positive. Make both positive and negative string paths equal in conductor size and length, identify A and B permanently, and prove OFF / 1 / 2 / BOTH selector behavior with all charge sources and loads disabled.

With modules covered, build two independent two-panel series strings. Uncover and measure about 100.8 V Voc at 25°C on each string separately; confirm close agreement, polarity, labels and isolation before landing their separate 4 mm² home runs. Parallel them only at the protected building-entry terminals, then confirm the SmartSolar's 100 A protected battery branch before closing the 40 A PV disconnect.

Commission the normal two-run PV configuration first and record current from each string. If cable shortage forces the one-run contingency, move the parallel point to the weatherproof protected array box using the supplied links, confirm the installed 4 mm² cable's ampacity is at least 40 A under the actual temperature/grouping method, use terminals rated for the combined current, and record the expected 4.04% STC cable loss. Do not use an improvised MC4 Y lead on the combined run.

Program MultiPlus and SmartSolar for the exact GEL label; planning values are 28.2 V absorption, 27.2 V float and equalization disabled. Install the temperature sensor supplied with the 24 V MultiPlus and set the Ekrano/DVCC system-wide charge-current limit to 100 A with both strings healthy.
Set the MultiPlus to 230 V / 50 Hz with a 10 A AC input-current limit for the G3200P; verify generator acceptance before enabling unattended charging.

Configure the Orion in power-supply mode with an initial 24.0 V input lockout and 25.0 V restart, then validate under the actual essential load and exact battery specification. Verify that recovery occurs only after meaningful recharge.

With the 24 V bank isolated, make a full-size enclosure layout and clearance mock-up. Mount the Ekrano horizontally through the 13.8 × 9.7 inch door using its rear steel bracket and compressed seal; fit the selector beside it, bond the Ekrano protective-earth terminal and keep every rear connector inside the dry box.

Power the Ekrano directly from the protected 24 V bus with its supplied 3.15 A slow-blow fused lead, with negative on the system side of the SmartShunt. Never power it from MultiPlus AC-out or from the voltage-controlled DC-load branch.

Connect the MultiPlus by Victron RJ45 UTP/VE.Bus, SmartSolar and SmartShunt by separate VE.Direct cables, and Ekrano Ethernet to the UniFi Express LAN port. Confirm all three devices and the SmartShunt battery state appear locally.

Register the Ekrano in VRM over UniFi/Starlink, enable HTTPS and two-factor authentication on administrator accounts, configure useful battery/temperature/offline alarms, set a connection-appropriate log interval, and test both local operation without internet and remote recovery after reconnect.
Set the Ekrano display auto-off timer and adaptive brightness, record the VRM Portal ID and access recovery details off-site, and export configuration backups before departure.
Torque to each manufacturer specification; re-torque after the first week and mark fasteners with witness paint.

Have a qualified electrical person test RCBO trip time, polarity, the continuous protective-earth path, lead strain relief, trailing-socket wiring and neutral-earth behavior in both inverter and generator/bypass modes. There are no fixed workshop wall outlets.
Connect Starlink Ethernet directly to the UniFi Express WAN port, reserve one 5 V / 3 A USB-C output for it, export a UniFi backup and test Wi-Fi with all other network equipment removed.

Run the 1,800 W saw alone for 30 minutes in warm conditions with the 3 m lead fully uncoiled while monitoring inverter, lead, plug/socket, cable and terminal temperature; post the one-page operating rules and fuse map beside the equipment.
